tasks.title: Upper limit of an I²C pull-up
tasks.solution: t_r = 0.8473·Rp·Cb (the 30→70 % edge), so Rp_max = t_r/(0.8473·Cb); ns/pF = kΩ. The lower limit at 3.3 V is 967 Ω; if Rp_max comes out smaller, the bus is impossible at this clock.

tasks.title: I²C line edge
tasks.solution: t_r = 0.8473·R·C; kΩ·pF = ns. Compare with 300 ns (400 kHz) and 1000 ns (100 kHz): 4.7 kΩ at 100 pF gives 398 ns, already too much for 400 kHz.

tasks.title: UART load from a GPS stream
tasks.solution: 10 bits per byte (start + 8 + stop): load = N·f·10/B. UBX-NAV-PVT is 100 bytes with the header: at 9600 baud and 10 Hz that is 104 %, at 115200 it is 8.7 %. Above 100 % the stream does not fit on the line and messages are lost.
